checks: Read q26_inject.log: injection with no fall gives binned R32/R21 0.91/0.91/0.89/0.86; 15% fall gives 0.84/0.86/0.85/0.83; core-removed fit recovers 1.01+-0.08 and 0.89+-0.08 (truth 0.85). Matches the summary and report.json. Agree the method is unbiased and the binned 0.85 'fall' is mostly core leakage.

Read q26_boot.log: R_ext ratio 1.05 (10in, u>8, Xb4f), 1.01 (u>10), 0.87/0.77 (6in), 1.26/1.38 (15in), boot sd 0.18-0.69. Agree with the adopted 1.0 +0.3/-0.4. The Xb4d set is systematically low (R_ext32=0.34-0.37 vs 0.49-0.67 for Xb4f, ratio 0.6-0.7), a ~35% EB-set discrepancy that is the dominant systematic. It is correctly folded into the lower error bar rather than hidden.
RADEX grid (q26_radex.log): expected R32/R21 0.5-0.93, typically 0.7-0.85. Consistent with the quoted range. The conclusion 'data cannot discriminate' is calibrated and honest.
Conventions: matched kilo-lambda, restored visibilities, core subtraction in the fit, and errors from bootstrap rather than formal sigma. All appropriate.
notes_for_questioner: Publish Q26 as a constraint, not a detection: R_ext(3-2)/R_ext(2-1) = 1.0 +0.3/-0.4 (about >0.65 at 2 sigma), no evidence of J-dependence, and no discrimination between sub-thermal and thermalised extended gas. State explicitly that the Xb4f vs Xb4d discrepancy (~35%) is unresolved and may be calibration/flux scale or short-baseline coverage. Follow-ups: (1) why Xb4d and Xb4f disagree in R_ext32. Compare the flux scale on common baselines and the calibrator fluxes. (2) A velocity-window and off-line control test. (3) Short-spacing 3-2 data (ACA) would be the decisive observation; propose it in the report. (4) Injection noise should use the real 2-5x scatter if it is rerun.
